本文は結びで、買われているのが物ではなく機会なら棚より卓が重要で新作の減少にも生き延び、人を呼んでいるのが棚なら部屋は空いていく、と二つの場合に分け、決着はこの部屋でつくと述べる。正解はこの条件分けを言い換えている。
【根拠】If what is being bought is an occasion rather than an object, the tables matter more than the shelves, and the business will outlive any fall in the number of new titles.
【他の選択肢】
① Their survival rests on publishers bringing out more titles every year, since visitors come chiefly to see whatever has just been released. … "Their survival rests on publishers bringing out more titles every year" — 本文は新作が減っても生き延びうる場合を示しており、新作の増加を存続の条件とする説明は本文と逆である。
② They will close once the novelty passes, because no business can live on the small sums a table of guests is prepared to spend in an evening. … "They will close once the novelty passes" — これは本文が紹介する批判側の見方にすぎず、本文はもう一方の見方を並べて結論を条件つきにしている。
④ They have already shown that they can take the place of ordinary shops, and the only question left is how soon the older sort will disappear. … "They have already shown that they can take the place of ordinary shops" — 既存の店に取って代わったという記述は本文になく、本文が扱うのは続くかどうかという未決の問いである。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文 内容一致
passages.title: Hunting in the Dark
passages.body:
After sunset a small insect-eating bat leaves its roost and hunts in air too dark for eyes to be useful. The familiar idea that it manages this because it is blind rests on a false premise, since no bat is actually blind. What lets them work in darkness is a second channel of information: the animal shouts as it flies, in pulses far too high for people to hear, and listens for the faint copies that come back from whatever lies ahead.

A returning echo carries more than the bare news that something is there. The gap between a call and its echo gives the distance, because sound moves through still air at a steady speed. The strength of the echo hints at the size of the object and the way it is spread out in time hints at the shape, since a beating wing answers differently from a leaf or a wall. Set one echo beside the next and the hunter can tell whether its target is closing or slipping away.

All of this depends on hearing a whisper immediately after producing a shout. The calls leave the mouth loud enough to injure the animal's own hearing if nothing were done, and the echo that follows a moment later is very much fainter. The solution is a matter of timing: a small muscle in the middle ear tightens just as each call is released, damping the ear's response, and lets go again before the echo arrives. Calling and listening are therefore not simultaneous but alternate, many times a second.

The insects have not stayed still either. Many night-flying moths carry simple ears tuned to the range of pitches the hunters use, and a moth that picks up a distant call turns and flies away from it, while one that hears a call close behind may fold its wings and drop. Certain moths answer with rapid clicks of their own, which appear to interfere with the hunter's reading of the echo, and a bat that has been clicked at often breaks off its attack.

A harder problem arises when a whole colony pours out of one cave at dusk, so that every animal flies through a storm of calls that are not its own. Bats in such crowds have been seen to shift the pitch of their calls away from those of their neighbors, which makes their own echoes easier to pick out. None of this is a single clever trick. It is a set of adjustments, in the voice, in the ear and in the flight path, that together turn darkness into a place where an animal can hunt as though it could see.
passages.body_ja:
日が沈むと、小さな食虫性のコウモリはねぐらを離れ、目では役に立たないほど暗い空を狩り場にする。目が見えないからそれができるのだという世間一般の考えは前提からして誤りで、目の見えないコウモリはいない。暗闇で活動できるのは第二の情報経路があるからだ。飛びながら声を出すのだが、その音は人間には高すぎて聞こえず、前方にあるものから返ってくるかすかな写しに耳を澄ませているのである。

返ってくる反射は、そこに何かがあるという事実だけを運んでくるのではない。声と反射の間隔は距離を教える。静かな空気の中を音が一定の速さで進むからだ。反射の強さは対象の大きさを、それが時間の中でどう広がっているかは形を示唆する。羽ばたく翅は、葉や壁とは違う返し方をするからである。一つの反射をその次の反射と並べれば、狙った相手が近づいているのか遠ざかっているのかまで分かる。

こうしたことはすべて、大声を出した直後にささやきを聞き取れるかどうかにかかっている。声は口を出る時点で、何もしなければ自分の聴覚を傷めるほど大きく、その少し後に返る反射ははるかに弱い。解決はタイミングにある。中耳の小さな筋肉が声を出すのと同時に締まって耳の反応を鈍らせ、反射が届く前にまた緩むのだ。つまり発声と聴取は同時ではなく、一秒に何度も交互に起きている。

昆虫の側も手をこまねいてはいない。夜に飛ぶ蛾の多くは、狩る側が使う音の高さの範囲に合わせた単純な耳を備えていて、遠くの声を捉えた蛾は向きを変えてそこから離れ、すぐ後ろで声を聞いた蛾は翅をたたんで落ちることもある。自分のほうから速いクリック音を返す蛾もいて、その音は狩る側の反射の読み取りを妨げるらしく、クリック音を浴びせられたコウモリはしばしば攻撃をやめてしまう。

もっと厄介な問題は、夕暮れに群れ全体が一つの洞窟から流れ出すときに起きる。どの個体も自分のものではない声の嵐の中を飛ぶことになるからだ。そうした混雑の中のコウモリは、声の高さを近くの仲間からずらすことが観察されており、そうすると自分の反射を拾い出しやすくなる。これは一つの巧妙な仕掛けなどではない。声と耳と飛び方における調整のひとそろいであり、それらが合わさって暗闇を、見えているかのように狩りのできる場所に変えているのである。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about how insect-eating bats find their way at night?
choices: Their eyes have grown so weak over time that they are effectively blind, and they must depend on sound for every part of the hunt.
They can see well enough, but in darkness they locate things by making sounds people cannot hear and reading what comes back to them.
They follow the faint noises that flying insects make with their wings, which is why they hunt best on nights that are calm and quiet.
They learn the layout of the ground around the roost in daylight and afterward keep to the routes they have already flown in the dark.
questions.explanation:
正解 ② They can see well enough, but in darkness they locate things by making sounds people cannot hear and reading what comes back to them.
本文は「目が見えないからだという通念は前提が誤りで、目の見えないコウモリはいない」と述べたうえで、暗闇で使えるのは第二の情報経路、すなわち人には高すぎて聞こえない音を出し、返ってくる反射を聞き取ることだと説明している。正解はこの二点をそのまま言い換えている。
【根拠】The familiar idea that it manages this because it is blind rests on a false premise, since no bat is actually blind. What lets them work in darkness is a second channel of information: the animal shouts as it flies, in pulses far too high for people to hear, and listens for the faint copies that come back from whatever lies ahead.
【他の選択肢】
① Their eyes have grown so weak over time that they are effectively blind, and they must depend on sound for every part of the hunt. … "Their eyes have grown so weak over time that they are effectively blind" — 本文は no bat is actually blind と明言しており、目が見えないという説明は本文と正反対。
③ They follow the faint noises that flying insects make with their wings, which is why they hunt best on nights that are calm and quiet. … "They follow the faint noises that flying insects make with their wings" — 本文で聞き取るのは自分が出した音の反射であって、獲物が出す音ではない。静かな夜がよいという話も本文にない。
④ They learn the layout of the ground around the roost in daylight and afterward keep to the routes they have already flown in the dark. … "They learn the layout of the ground around the roost in daylight" — 昼間に地形を覚えて飛ぶという記述は本文のどこにもなく、暗闇での方法として本文が挙げているものとも別。

questions.stem: What role does a small muscle in a bat's middle ear play while the animal is hunting?
choices: It keeps the ear wide open from the first call to the last so that no part of any returning echo can be missed during a chase.
It steadies the head while the animal is turning sharply, a task that becomes more difficult as the speed of the chase increases.
It lifts the pitch of every call beyond the range that flying insects are able to detect, so that the approach stays hidden from them.
The animal's own voice is loud enough to damage its hearing, so the ear is shielded for an instant and opened again in time for the weak reply.
questions.explanation:
正解 ④ The animal's own voice is loud enough to damage its hearing, so the ear is shielded for an instant and opened again in time for the weak reply.
本文は、鳴き声はそのままでは自分の聴覚を傷めるほど大きく、直後に返る反射ははるかに弱いと述べ、その解決が「発声と同時に中耳の筋肉が締まって感度を落とし、反射が届く前に緩む」というタイミングだと説明している。正解はこの因果をそのまま言い換えている。
【根拠】The calls leave the mouth loud enough to injure the animal's own hearing if nothing were done, and the echo that follows a moment later is very much fainter. The solution is a matter of timing: a small muscle in the middle ear tightens just as each call is released, damping the ear's response, and lets go again before the echo arrives.
【他の選択肢】
① It keeps the ear wide open from the first call to the last so that no part of any returning echo can be missed during a chase. … "It keeps the ear wide open from the first call to the last" — 本文では筋肉は発声のたびに耳の反応を damping する、つまり一時的に感度を落とす。耳を開いたままにするという説明は本文と逆。
② It steadies the head while the animal is turning sharply, a task that becomes more difficult as the speed of the chase increases. … "It steadies the head while the animal is turning sharply" — 頭部の安定や旋回速度についての記述は本文になく、中耳の筋肉の働きとして述べられている内容とも無関係。
③ It lifts the pitch of every call beyond the range that flying insects are able to detect, so that the approach stays hidden from them. … "It lifts the pitch of every call beyond the range that flying insects are able to detect" — 本文では蛾の耳はコウモリが使う音域に合っていると述べられており、獲物に気づかれない高さにするという説明は本文に反する。

questions.stem: What does the writer conclude about the way these animals deal with darkness?
choices: Once one specialized ability had appeared, every other change in the animals became unnecessary, since that ability alone settles the problem of hunting without light.
Only the individuals that hunt on their own can use sound successfully, because crowded air makes the whole method useless for the members of a large colony.
Several separate adjustments, in the calls they produce, in what their ears do and in how they fly, work together to make hunting without light possible.
Their success rests mainly on how loud the calls are, since the volume drowns out the sounds made by the insects they happen to be chasing.
questions.explanation:
正解 ③ Several separate adjustments, in the calls they produce, in what their ears do and in how they fly, work together to make hunting without light possible.
本文は末尾で「これは一つの巧妙な仕掛けではない」と否定し、声・耳・飛び方という複数の調整が合わさって暗闇を狩りの場に変えていると結論づける。正解はこの複数要素の組み合わせという結論を言い換えている。
【根拠】None of this is a single clever trick. It is a set of adjustments, in the voice, in the ear and in the flight path, that together turn darkness into a place where an animal can hunt as though it could see.
【他の選択肢】
① Once one specialized ability had appeared, every other change in the animals became unnecessary, since that ability alone settles the problem of hunting without light. … "Once one specialized ability had appeared, every other change in the animals became unnecessary" — 本文は None of this is a single clever trick と明言しており、単一の能力で片づくという主張とは逆。
② Only the individuals that hunt on their own can use sound successfully, because crowded air makes the whole method useless for the members of a large colony. … "Only the individuals that hunt on their own can use sound successfully" — 本文は群れで飛ぶときに声の高さをずらして混信を避けると述べており、集団では方法が使えないという説明は本文に反する。
④ Their success rests mainly on how loud the calls are, since the volume drowns out the sounds made by the insects they happen to be chasing. … "Their success rests mainly on how loud the calls are" — 声の大きさは本文に出てくるが、それは自分の聴覚を守る必要の理由として挙げられているだけで、獲物の音をかき消すためでも成功の主因でもない。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文 内容一致
passages.title: Pen or Keyboard
passages.body:
In any hall where a lecture is under way, the room has already divided itself in two. Some have a notebook open and a pen moving across it; the rest sit behind a screen with their fingers on a keyboard. Teachers argue about whether the difference matters, and a few have gone as far as shutting laptops out of their rooms. The argument deserves a careful hearing, because the honest answer is messier than either side usually admits.

The plainest difference between the two methods is speed. Most students type faster than they write by hand, and the quicker the fingers move, the closer the record comes to being a copy of everything the speaker said. A pen cannot keep up, so the person holding one has to decide, sentence by sentence, what is worth keeping and how to compress it. That decision is not a cost of handwriting but the main thing it offers: the material has to be understood before it can be shortened.

The idea has been put to the test. In an experiment that is often quoted, students who wrote their notes by hand and students who typed them did about equally well on questions asking for facts, while those who had used a pen did better on questions asking them to explain an idea. Later attempts to repeat the work, however, have not always found the same gap, and its size appears to depend on such things as how much time passed before the test.

What happens after the lecture may matter more than what happens during it. Typed notes can be searched in a moment, read by anybody and sent to a classmate who was ill, while handwritten pages take arrows, sketches and remarks in the margin, though hunting for one line in a term's worth of them is slow. Either way, the value of a set of notes is settled on the second pass, when the person who made them comes back to them, and pages that are never opened again help nobody.

Schools meet a narrower version of the same argument. The hours available for teaching are fixed, so time spent on forming letters neatly is time taken from something else, and instruction in handwriting has been cut back in many places. Against that, teachers point out that a pen never runs out of power, that a lit screen pulls at its owner and at the students behind, and that in many schools the papers that decide a pupil's future are still written by hand.

Put together, all of this points away from the question most people ask. A student who types a summary in their own words is doing what the pen forces on its user, and a student who copies a lecture word for word by hand gains little from the slower tool. What separates the two halves of the hall is not the object in front of them but whether anything is being chosen, and a rule that takes away one tool leaves that habit exactly where it was.
passages.body_ja:
講義が行われている教室なら、どこでも部屋はすでに二つに分かれている。ノートを開いてペンを走らせている学生がいる一方で、残りは画面の向こうに座り、指をキーボードに置いている。この違いに意味があるのかどうかで教師たちは論じ合い、なかにはノートパソコンを教室から締め出すところまで行った者もいる。この議論は丁寧に聞く価値がある。正直な答えは、どちらの側がふつう認めるよりも込み入っているからだ。

二つの方法のいちばん分かりやすい違いは速さである。たいていの学生は手で書くよりも速く打てるし、指が速く動くほど、記録は話し手の言ったことすべての写しに近づいていく。ペンは追いつけないので、ペンを持つ側は一文ごとに、何を残す価値があり、どう縮めるかを決めなければならない。この判断は手書きの代償ではなく、手書きが差し出す当のものである。縮めるには、まず中身を理解していなければならないからだ。

この考えは実際に検証されている。よく引き合いに出される実験では、ノートを手で書いた学生と打ち込んだ学生は、事実を問う設問ではほぼ同等の出来だったが、考えを説明させる設問ではペンを使ったほうがよくできた。もっとも、その後の追試では同じ差が常に見つかるわけではなく、差の大きさは、試験までにどれだけ時間が空いたかといった事情に左右されるらしい。

講義の最中よりも、講義の後に何が起きるかのほうが重要かもしれない。打ち込んだノートはすぐに検索でき、誰にでも読め、欠席した級友に送ることもできる。一方、手書きのページは矢印や図や余白の書き込みを受け入れるが、一学期分の中から一行を探し出すのは骨が折れる。どちらにせよ、ノートの価値は二度目に目を通すとき、つまり作った本人がそこへ戻ってきたときに決まるのであって、二度と開かれないページは誰の役にも立たない。

学校はこれと同じ議論の、もっと範囲の狭い形に直面する。授業に使える時間は決まっているので、字を整えて書く練習に充てた時間は別の何かから取った時間になり、手書きの指導は多くの地域で削られてきた。これに対して教師たちは、ペンは電池が切れないこと、光る画面は持ち主にも後ろに座る学生にも気を引くこと、そして多くの学校で生徒の進路を決める答案は今なお手で書かれることを指摘する。

こうしてまとめてみると、以上のすべては、多くの人が立てる問いとは別の方向を指している。自分の言葉で要約を打ち込む学生は、ペンがその使い手に強いるのと同じことをしているし、講義を一語一語手で書き写す学生は、遅い道具からほとんど得ていない。教室の二つの側を分けているのは目の前にある物ではなく、何かが選び取られているかどうかであり、片方の道具を取り上げる規則は、その習慣をそっくりそのままにしておくのである。

questions.stem: According to the passage, why can taking notes with a pen be an advantage?
choices: Because the hand is too slow to catch everything, the writer has to judge what matters and say it in fewer words, which cannot be done without understanding it.
Because a pen moves just as quickly as a keyboard does, students who use one finish with a record of the lecture that is every bit as complete.
Because writing by hand makes no noise, the students seated nearby are able to give their attention to the speaker instead of to the room around them.
Because handwritten pages are hard to search through later, students who use a pen have no choice but to memorize the lecture while it is going on.
questions.explanation:
正解 ① Because the hand is too slow to catch everything, the writer has to judge what matters and say it in fewer words, which cannot be done without understanding it.
本文は、ペンは話す速さに追いつけないので書く側は一文ごとに何を残し、どう縮めるかを判断しなければならず、その判断こそ手書きの利点であり、縮めるには内容を理解している必要があると述べる。正解はこの因果関係を言い換えている。
【根拠】A pen cannot keep up, so the person holding one has to decide, sentence by sentence, what is worth keeping and how to compress it. That decision is not a cost of handwriting but the main thing it offers: the material has to be understood before it can be shortened.
【他の選択肢】
② Because a pen moves just as quickly as a keyboard does, students who use one finish with a record of the lecture that is every bit as complete. … "Because a pen moves just as quickly as a keyboard does" — 本文は Most students type faster than they write by hand と述べており、速さが同じだという前提は本文に反する。
③ Because writing by hand makes no noise, the students seated nearby are able to give their attention to the speaker instead of to the room around them. … "Because writing by hand makes no noise" — 打鍵音や教室の静けさについての記述は本文になく、手書きの利点として挙げられているものとも別。
④ Because handwritten pages are hard to search through later, students who use a pen have no choice but to memorize the lecture while it is going on. … "students who use a pen have no choice but to memorize the lecture while it is going on" — 検索しにくい点は本文にあるが、そこから講義中に暗記するという話にはつながらず、本文が述べる利点は判断して縮めることである。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the research comparing the two kinds of note-takers?
choices: The two groups came out level on questions about facts but not on questions calling for explanation, and later work has not always found that difference again.
It showed that the students using keyboards did worse on every type of question, and every study carried out since has confirmed that result without exception.
It found no difference at all between the two groups, and the writer uses it to argue that the choice of tool has never been worth discussing.
It was run only on students who had already been trained to take notes in one particular way, so its result says nothing about ordinary classes.
questions.explanation:
正解 ① The two groups came out level on questions about facts but not on questions calling for explanation, and later work has not always found that difference again.
本文は、事実を問う設問では両群がほぼ同等で、考えを説明させる設問では手書き群のほうがよかったと述べ、さらに後の追試では同じ差が常に出るわけではないと続ける。正解はこの二段構えをそのまま言い換えている。
【根拠】In an experiment that is often quoted, students who wrote their notes by hand and students who typed them did about equally well on questions asking for facts, while those who had used a pen did better on questions asking them to explain an idea. Later attempts to repeat the work, however, have not always found the same gap, and its size appears to depend on such things as how much time passed before the test.
【他の選択肢】
② It showed that the students using keyboards did worse on every type of question, and every study carried out since has confirmed that result without exception. … "the students using keyboards did worse on every type of question" — 本文では事実を問う設問では両群が about equally well であり、すべての設問で劣っていたという記述は本文に反する。
③ It found no difference at all between the two groups, and the writer uses it to argue that the choice of tool has never been worth discussing. … "It found no difference at all between the two groups" — 本文は説明を求める設問で差が出たと述べており、差がなかったという説明は本文と逆。
④ It was run only on students who had already been trained to take notes in one particular way, so its result says nothing about ordinary classes. … "It was run only on students who had already been trained to take notes in one particular way" — 参加者が特定の取り方の訓練を受けていたという記述は本文になく、本文が触れているのは追試で同じ差が常には出ないことである。

questions.stem: What does the writer mean by "the second pass"?
choices: The point in a lecture at which a speaker says an important thing over again so that anyone who missed it the first time can get it down.
The later occasion on which students go back over the notes they made, which is where the writer says the worth of those notes is decided.
The habit of borrowing a classmate's notes after the lecture in order to fill in the parts that were missed while the speaker was talking.
The second of the two tools described in the passage, that is, the keyboard, which the writer treats as the newer arrival in the classroom.
questions.explanation:
正解 ② The later occasion on which students go back over the notes they made, which is where the writer says the worth of those notes is decided.
本文は「どちらの方法でも、ノートの価値は the second pass で決まる」と述べ、直後に when the person who made them comes back to them と説明を添え、二度と開かれないページは役に立たないと続ける。したがってこの語句は後から自分のノートを読み返す機会を指す。
【根拠】Either way, the value of a set of notes is settled on the second pass, when the person who made them comes back to them, and pages that are never opened again help nobody.
【他の選択肢】
① The point in a lecture at which a speaker says an important thing over again so that anyone who missed it the first time can get it down. … "The point in a lecture at which a speaker says an important thing over again" — 本文の語句は講義中の出来事ではなく、ノートを作った本人が後から戻ってくる場面を指している。
③ The habit of borrowing a classmate's notes after the lecture in order to fill in the parts that were missed while the speaker was talking. … "The habit of borrowing a classmate's notes after the lecture" — 本文で級友に関わるのは、打ち込んだノートを欠席者に送れるという別の箇所であり、この語句の説明ではない。
④ The second of the two tools described in the passage, that is, the keyboard, which the writer treats as the newer arrival in the classroom. … "The second of the two tools described in the passage, that is, the keyboard" — この語句は道具ではなく回数を表しており、本文は直後に comes back to them と述べて読み返す機会であることを明示している。

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the writer's conclusion?
choices: Laptops ought to be kept out of classrooms, since no student who works on one can obtain the benefit that the slower tool gives to the people who use it.
Because the papers that decide a pupil's future are still handwritten, schools should give back to handwriting all the hours it used to receive in the timetable.
What counts is whether the note-taker is selecting rather than copying, so a rule that removes one of the tools does not touch the difference that actually matters.
The research has settled the question in favor of the pen, and students who work on a keyboard are at a disadvantage whatever they later do with their notes.
questions.explanation:
正解 ③ What counts is whether the note-taker is selecting rather than copying, so a rule that removes one of the tools does not touch the difference that actually matters.
本文は結びで、教室の二つの側を分けるのは目の前の道具ではなく何かが選び取られているかどうかであり、道具を取り上げる規則はその習慣に手を触れないと述べる。正解はこの結論を言い換えている。
【根拠】What separates the two halves of the hall is not the object in front of them but whether anything is being chosen, and a rule that takes away one tool leaves that habit exactly where it was.
【他の選択肢】
① Laptops ought to be kept out of classrooms, since no student who works on one can obtain the benefit that the slower tool gives to the people who use it. … "Laptops ought to be kept out of classrooms" — 本文は自分の言葉で要約を打ち込む学生はペンが強いるのと同じことをしていると述べており、道具を締め出せという主張とは逆。
② Because the papers that decide a pupil's future are still handwritten, schools should give back to handwriting all the hours it used to receive in the timetable. … "schools should give back to handwriting all the hours it used to receive" — 手書きで答案を書く学校が多いことは教師側の指摘として出てくるだけで、授業時間を元に戻せという主張は本文にない。
④ The research has settled the question in favor of the pen, and students who work on a keyboard are at a disadvantage whatever they later do with their notes. … "The research has settled the question in favor of the pen" — 本文は追試で同じ差が常に出るわけではないと述べており、研究が決着をつけたという説明は本文に反する。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文 内容一致
passages.title: Spotting Smoke Before It Spreads
passages.body:
A fire in dry forest country is cheap to stop in its first minutes and ruinously expensive a few hours later. For a long time the answer was a line of wooden towers on high ground, each with a watcher who searched the horizon all season for a smudge that had not been there before. The towers worked, but they were costly to staff, they covered only what could be seen from them, and they asked a person to stay alert through weeks in which nothing happened.

Many of the ridges that once held towers now hold cameras that turn through a full circle every few minutes and send their pictures to software trained on stored images of real fires. What that software looks for is not a color. A single still frame of gray against gray says almost nothing, so the program compares each picture with the ones before it and waits for a pale mass that widens, climbs, and leans away with the wind. Some networks add sensors among the trees to measure particles in the air, and most services still take calls from the public. The three sources are kept because they fail in different ways.

Any such network is generous with warnings. Dust from a truck on a logging track, mist lifting off a valley floor after rain, and steam from a mill chimney all produce a rising column that a camera cannot separate from the start of a fire. It would be easy enough to make the system harder to satisfy, but a threshold high enough to shut out dust and mist would also shut out the thin early smoke the network was built to find. So the warnings go to an operator, who decides whether to send anyone at all. A crew standing in a clearing beside a dusty track is a crew that cannot answer the next call.

Landscape sets the other limit. A fire deep in a steep valley can burn unnoticed until it reaches a ridge line, by which time the cheap hours are gone. On heavy, windless mornings the smoke sometimes spreads sideways in a flat layer instead of rising, and the shape the software expects never appears. Sensors under the trees answer part of this, but they need power and a signal, both thin in the country that burns.

None of this makes the old towers worth rebuilding. What these networks have changed is not that people have stopped watching but where the watching is done, and the whole case for building them rests on a handful of minutes at the start.
passages.body_ja:
乾いた森林地帯の火事は、最初の数分なら安く止められるが、数時間たてば法外な費用がかかる。長いあいだ、その答えは高台に並ぶ木造の塔だった。塔にはそれぞれ見張りが一人いて、季節のあいだじゅう、それまでそこになかった煙の汚れを地平線に探し続けた。塔は役に立った。だが人を置き続けるには費用がかかり、覆えるのはそこから見える範囲だけで、しかも何も起こらない週を何週も、人に注意を保ち続けることを求めるものでもあった。

かつて塔が立っていた尾根の多くには、今はカメラがある。カメラは数分ごとに一周し、実際の火災を写した保存画像で学習させたソフトウェアへ画像を送る。そのソフトが探しているのは色ではない。灰色の中の灰色を写した一枚の静止画ではほとんど何も分からないので、プログラムは各画像を直前の画像と比べ、広がり、立ち上り、風に流されていく淡いかたまりが現れるのを待つ。網によっては木立の中にセンサーを置いて大気中の粒子を測るものもあり、たいていの機関は今でも市民からの電話を受けている。三つの情報源を併せて残してあるのは、それぞれ違うかたちで失敗するからだ。

この種の網はどれも警報を出し過ぎる。伐採路を走るトラックが立てるほこり、雨あがりに谷底から立ちのぼる霧、工場の煙突から出る蒸気は、どれも立ち上る柱を作り、カメラはそれを火事の始まりと区別できない。判定を厳しくするのは造作もないが、ほこりや霧を締め出せるだけの高さのしきい値は、この網が見つけるために作られた初期の薄い煙まで締め出してしまう。そこで警報は担当者のもとへ送られ、担当者がそもそも人を出すかどうかを決める。ほこりっぽい道ばたの空き地に立っている隊は、次の通報に応じられない隊である。

もう一つの限界は地形が決める。深く切れ込んだ谷の奥で始まった火は、尾根筋に達するまで気づかれずに燃えることがあり、その時点で安く済む時間は過ぎている。重く風のない朝には、煙が立ち上らずに平らな層のまま横へ広がることがあり、ソフトが待ち受けている形はついに現れない。木の下のセンサーはこの一部に応えるが、電源と電波が要る。そしてその二つは、まさによく燃える土地でこそ乏しい。

だからといって古い塔を建て直す価値が生まれるわけではない。この網が変えたのは、人が見張るのをやめたということではなく、どこで見張るかということであり、建設を正当化する根拠はすべて、初動のわずか数分にかかっている。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the way the software decides that it may be looking at smoke?
choices: It sets each picture against the ones taken before it and waits for a pale shape that spreads and moves, because one frame alone tells it very little.
It measures the color of the air above the tree line and reports any reading that differs from the one it recorded on the previous day.
It waits for the sensors among the trees to record particles in the air and only then begins to examine the pictures the camera has sent.
It treats every rising column as a fire and leaves the work of separating smoke from dust to the crews once they arrive on the ground.
questions.explanation:
正解 ① It sets each picture against the ones taken before it and waits for a pale shape that spreads and moves, because one frame alone tells it very little.
本文は、灰色の中の灰色を写した一枚の静止画ではほとんど何も分からないため、プログラムは各画像を直前の画像と比べ、広がり・上昇し・風に流れる淡いかたまりを待つ、と述べている。正解はこの「連続した画像の比較」と「広がって動く形」を言い換えている。
【根拠】A single still frame of gray against gray says almost nothing, so the program compares each picture with the ones before it and waits for a pale mass that widens, climbs, and leans away with the wind.
【他の選択肢】
② It measures the color of the air above the tree line and reports any reading that differs from the one it recorded on the previous day. … "It measures the color of the air above the tree line" — 本文は What that software looks for is not a color. と明言しており、色を測って判断するという記述は本文にない。
③ It waits for the sensors among the trees to record particles in the air and only then begins to examine the pictures the camera has sent. … "It waits for the sensors among the trees to record particles ... and only then begins to examine the pictures" — センサーは一部の網が加える補助であり、画像の判定がセンサーの後に行われるという順序は本文にない。
④ It treats every rising column as a fire and leaves the work of separating smoke from dust to the crews once they arrive on the ground. … "leaves the work of separating smoke from dust to the crews once they arrive on the ground" — 本文で煙とほこりを見分けて出動の可否を決めるのは警報を受け取る operator であり、現場に着いた隊員に任せるとは書かれていない。

questions.stem: Why is the detection system not simply set so that it sends out fewer warnings?
choices: Because the services that run it are required to pass on every warning it produces, whatever the operator believes the cause to be.
Because a setting strict enough to keep out dust and mist would also keep out the faint early smoke the network exists to catch.
Because operators have found that a crew reaches a fire faster when it has already been called out several times earlier in the week.
Because the sensors among the trees remove most of the doubtful warnings before anything at all reaches the operator on duty.
questions.explanation:
正解 ② Because a setting strict enough to keep out dust and mist would also keep out the faint early smoke the network exists to catch.
本文は、判定を厳しくするのは簡単だが、ほこりや霧を締め出せる高さのしきい値は、この網が見つけるために作られた初期の薄い煙まで締め出してしまう、と述べている。正解はこの二者択一の理由をそのまま言い換えている。
【根拠】It would be easy enough to make the system harder to satisfy, but a threshold high enough to shut out dust and mist would also shut out the thin early smoke the network was built to find.
【他の選択肢】
① Because the services that run it are required to pass on every warning it produces, whatever the operator believes the cause to be. … "the services that run it are required to pass on every warning it produces" — 警報をすべて転送する義務があるという規定は本文のどこにもなく、一般論にすぎない。
③ Because operators have found that a crew reaches a fire faster when it has already been called out several times earlier in the week. … "a crew reaches a fire faster when it has already been called out several times" — 出動回数が到着の速さを上げるという記述は本文にない。本文が挙げるのは、誤報で出た隊が次の通報に応じられなくなるという不利だけである。
④ Because the sensors among the trees remove most of the doubtful warnings before anything at all reaches the operator on duty. … "the sensors among the trees remove most of the doubtful warnings before anything at all reaches the operator on duty" — センサーは一部の網が加える補助で、疑わしい警報をふるい落とす装置としては書かれておらず、警報は operator のもとへ送られる。

questions.stem: What is the writer's overall view of these detection networks?
choices: They have shown that a watcher on high ground still sees more than any camera placed in the same spot, so the towers deserve to be put back.
They should be judged by the number of warnings they send in a season, since that figure shows how much ground they are able to cover.
They will do away with the need for human judgment as soon as the trouble caused by dust and mist has been dealt with.
They have moved human attention somewhere else rather than removed it, and their worth lies in the short time they save at the beginning.
questions.explanation:
正解 ④ They have moved human attention somewhere else rather than removed it, and their worth lies in the short time they save at the beginning.
本文は、変わったのは人が見張るのをやめたことではなく見張る場所であり、建設を正当化する根拠はすべて初動のわずかな数分にある、と述べている。正解は「人の仕事はなくならず移っただけ」「価値は初期に稼ぐ時間」という二点を言い換えている。
【根拠】What these networks have changed is not that people have stopped watching but where the watching is done, and the whole case for building them rests on a handful of minutes at the start.
【他の選択肢】
① They have shown that a watcher on high ground still sees more than any camera placed in the same spot, so the towers deserve to be put back. … "the towers deserve to be put back" — 本文は None of this makes the old towers worth rebuilding. と述べており、塔を戻すべきだという主張は本文と逆。
② They should be judged by the number of warnings they send in a season, since that figure shows how much ground they are able to cover. … "They should be judged by the number of warnings they send in a season" — 警報の件数で評価すべきだという基準は本文にない。本文はむしろ警報が多すぎること自体を問題として扱っている。
③ They will do away with the need for human judgment as soon as the trouble caused by dust and mist has been dealt with. … "They will do away with the need for human judgment" — 本文では最後に出動を決めるのは operator であり、人の判断が不要になるという見通しは示されていない。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文 内容一致
passages.title: One Sport or Many
passages.body:
A child who turns out to be good at a sport will sooner or later be asked to choose, though the request is rarely put as a choice. It arrives as a schedule: a club season that runs into the next, a camp in the school holidays, an extra session on Sunday. Behind it sits an assumption almost nobody states out loud, that hours spent in one sport before the teenage years buy an advantage the same hours spread across several sports cannot.

The clearest objection to that assumption comes from the medical side. A young body that repeats one motion all year loads the same joints, tendons, and growing tissues week after week, and it does so while those tissues are still forming. The injuries that follow are not dramatic but slow, beginning as a stiffness the player never mentions and ending in a season missed. A child who swims in one season and runs in another is not resting, but the parts under load change, and those that were loaded get the months they need.

The argument about improvement is less one-sided than either camp admits. Children who narrow early do often lead their age group at first, and that lead is what parents can see. What the coaches of older athletes report is that the gap tends to close, and that the qualities which decide matches later, such as balance, changing direction under pressure, and reading what a moving situation is about to become, are built as readily in one game as in another and carry across between them. In a few sports where the finest performances come at a young age an early start is hard to avoid.

The figures that get least attention are the ones about leaving. A large share of young players stop competing before they finish school, and what they say afterward has less to do with ability than with how the years felt: the sport had become an obligation, the enjoyment had gone, the friends had gone before them. Here the two paths separate. A child who has played several games can give one up and still have somewhere to be on a Saturday morning. A child who has played nothing else since primary school gives up the training, the coaches, the weekend routine, and most of the people they know, all at once. That second loss is the part no dropout figure records.

Coaches and parents do not stand in the same place when they weigh this up. A coach is handed a squad for a season and judged on what it does inside that season, which makes an extra winter of training an obvious good. A parent is the only person looking at a whole childhood. The advice that has settled out of the argument is modest: keep a second sport somewhere in the year, put a ceiling on the weekly hours in the main one, and leave a stretch of months clear of it. It is not a rule against choosing but a rule against closing the other doors while the child is still too young to know which one they will want.
passages.body_ja:
ある競技が得意だと分かった子どもは、遅かれ早かれ選ぶことを求められる。ただし、その求めが選択として示されることはめったにない。やってくるのは予定表である。次の季節へそのまま続くクラブのシーズン、学校の休みに組まれた合宿、日曜の追加練習。その背後には、ほとんど誰も口に出さない前提が置かれている。十代になる前に一つの競技に注いだ時間は、同じ時間をいくつかの競技に分けて使ったのでは得られない優位を買う、という前提である。

その前提に対する最も明確な反論は医学の側から出てくる。一年中同じ動作を繰り返す若い体は、同じ関節、腱、成長中の組織に毎週毎週負荷をかけ、しかもそれらの組織がまだ形を作っている最中にそうする。その結果起こるけがは、劇的ではなく緩慢で、本人が決して口にしないこわばりとして始まり、一季節を棒に振って終わる。ある季節には泳ぎ、別の季節には走る子どもは、休んでいるわけではない。しかし負荷のかかる部位が入れ替わり、それまで負荷を受けていた部位は必要な数か月を得る。

上達についての議論は、どちらの陣営が認めるよりも一方的ではない。早くに絞った子どもは確かに最初のうち同学年の先頭に立つことが多く、保護者の目に見えるのはその先行である。年長の選手を見ている指導者たちが報告するのは、その差は縮まる傾向があるということ、そして後年の試合を決める資質、たとえば平衡感覚、圧力の下で方向を変えること、動いている状況がこれからどうなるかを読むことは、どの競技でも同じように育ち、競技のあいだを越えて持ち越されるということである。最高の演技が若い年齢で出る少数の競技では、早い開始は避けにくい。

最も注目されない数字は、やめることについての数字である。若い選手のかなりの割合が学校を終える前に競技をやめており、彼らが後から語る理由は、能力よりも、その年月がどう感じられたかに関わっている。競技が義務になっていた、楽しさが消えていた、友人が先にいなくなっていた、というものだ。ここで二つの道は分かれる。いくつかの競技をしてきた子どもは、一つをやめてもなお土曜の朝に行く場所がある。小学校以来ほかに何もしてこなかった子どもは、練習も、指導者も、週末の生活の型も、知っている人のほとんどをも、一度に手放す。この二つ目の喪失こそ、どの離脱者の数字にも記録されない部分である。

これを量るとき、指導者と保護者は同じ場所に立っていない。指導者は一季節のあいだ選手団を預けられ、その季節の中で選手団が何をしたかで評価される。だから冬の練習が一つ増えることは当然の善に見える。子ども時代の全体を見ているのは保護者だけである。議論の末に落ち着いた助言は控えめなものだ。第二の競技を年のどこかに残すこと、主競技の週あたりの時間に上限を置くこと、そしてそれをまったくやらない数か月を空けておくこと。これは選ぶことを禁じる決まりではなく、どの扉を望むことになるか分からないほど子どもがまだ幼いうちに、ほかの扉を閉じてしまうことを禁じる決まりである。

questions.stem: According to the passage, why does staying in one sport all year raise the risk of injury for a young player?
choices: Because a player who trains all year is given tasks that are harder than the ones set for players who train for only part of it.
Because the same joints and growing tissues are worked week after week at an age when they have not yet finished forming.
Because the training done inside a single sport is more violent than the training done in a sport that is played for one season.
Because a player with no other sport will hide an injury in order to keep a place in the only squad that is open to them.
questions.explanation:
正解 ② Because the same joints and growing tissues are worked week after week at an age when they have not yet finished forming.
本文は、一年中同じ動作を繰り返す若い体は同じ関節・腱・成長中の組織に毎週負荷をかけ、しかもそれらの組織がまだ形成途中のときにそうする、と述べている。正解はこの「同じ部位への反復負荷」と「未成熟な時期」という二点を言い換えている。
【根拠】A young body that repeats one motion all year loads the same joints, tendons, and growing tissues week after week, and it does so while those tissues are still forming.
【他の選択肢】
① Because a player who trains all year is given tasks that are harder than the ones set for players who train for only part of it. … "is given tasks that are harder than the ones set for players who train for only part of it" — 練習内容の難度の差は本文にない。本文が問題にしているのは難度ではなく、負荷のかかる部位が変わらないことである。
③ Because the training done inside a single sport is more violent than the training done in a sport that is played for one season. … "the training done inside a single sport is more violent" — 単一競技の練習のほうが激しいという比較は本文になく、本文は激しさを理由に挙げていない。
④ Because a player with no other sport will hide an injury in order to keep a place in the only squad that is open to them. … "will hide an injury in order to keep a place in the only squad" — けがを隠すという行動は本文に出てこない。本文にあるのは、本人が口にしないこわばりから始まる緩慢なけがである。

questions.stem: What do the coaches of older athletes report about children who narrow down to one sport early?
choices: The lead they hold over others of the same age tends to disappear, and the abilities that settle later matches move freely between sports.
The lead they hold grows wider every year, which is why parents are advised to let a child settle on a single game before the teenage years.
They lose the balance and the sense of a moving game that children with several sports keep, and they never manage to recover either of them.
They reach their finest performances at a younger age than other players and are therefore obliged to leave competition earlier than the rest.
questions.explanation:
正解 ① The lead they hold over others of the same age tends to disappear, and the abilities that settle later matches move freely between sports.
本文は、年長の選手を見る指導者の報告として、差は縮まる傾向があり、後年の試合を決める資質はどの競技でも同じように育って競技間を越えて持ち越される、と述べている。正解はこの二点を言い換えている。
【根拠】What the coaches of older athletes report is that the gap tends to close, and that the qualities which decide matches later, such as balance, changing direction under pressure, and reading what a moving situation is about to become, are built as readily in one game as in another and carry across between them.
【他の選択肢】
② The lead they hold grows wider every year, which is why parents are advised to let a child settle on a single game before the teenage years. … "The lead they hold grows wider every year" — 本文は the gap tends to close と述べており、差が年々広がるというのは本文と逆。
③ They lose the balance and the sense of a moving game that children with several sports keep, and they never manage to recover either of them. … "They lose the balance and the sense of a moving game ... and they never manage to recover either of them" — 本文はそれらの資質がどの競技でも同じように育つと述べているだけで、早く絞った子がそれを失い二度と取り戻せないとは書かれていない。
④ They reach their finest performances at a younger age than other players and are therefore obliged to leave competition earlier than the rest. … "They reach their finest performances at a younger age than other players" — 若い年齢で最高の成績が出ると本文が述べているのは少数の競技についてであって、早く一競技に絞った子ども一般の話ではない。

questions.stem: What does the author mean by the phrase "That second loss"?
choices: The second injury that ends the career of a player who has already missed one whole season through the overuse of the same joints.
The money a family has already handed over to a single club, none of which comes back once the child stops taking part in it.
The fall in the number of young players a club can count on once its most promising members have moved to a different sport.
What a child gives up besides the sport itself, namely the weekly routine, the adults who ran it, and nearly everyone they spent time with.
questions.explanation:
正解 ④ What a child gives up besides the sport itself, namely the weekly routine, the adults who ran it, and nearly everyone they spent time with.
直前の文が、小学校以来ほかに何もしてこなかった子は、練習・指導者・週末の生活の型・知っている人のほとんどを一度に手放すと述べている。That second loss はこの、競技そのものをやめること以外に失われるもの全体を指している。
【根拠】A child who has played nothing else since primary school gives up the training, the coaches, the weekend routine, and most of the people they know, all at once.
【他の選択肢】
① The second injury that ends the career of a player who has already missed one whole season through the overuse of the same joints. … "The second injury that ends the career of a player" — 二度目のけがという話は本文になく、この段落が扱っているのはけがではなく競技から離れることである。
② The money a family has already handed over to a single club, none of which comes back once the child stops taking part in it. … "The money a family has already handed over to a single club" — 家庭が払った費用への言及は本文のどこにもない。
③ The fall in the number of young players a club can count on once its most promising members have moved to a different sport. … "The fall in the number of young players a club can count on" — 本文が問題にしているのはやめる子ども本人が失うものであって、クラブ側の人数の減少ではない。

questions.stem: What conclusion does the writer reach about how this question should be handled?
choices: Children should be kept out of organized competition altogether until they are old enough to explain why they want to take part in it.
Nothing forbids an early choice, but the other paths should be kept open while the child is still too young to know which one will matter.
The decision belongs to the coach, since only someone who sees the squad every week can say whether more training would help the player.
A child should be moved into a new sport every year so that no single set of joints is ever kept under load for more than one season.
questions.explanation:
正解 ② Nothing forbids an early choice, but the other paths should be kept open while the child is still too young to know which one will matter.
本文は末尾で、これは選ぶことを禁じる決まりではなく、どの扉を望むことになるか分からないほど子どもが幼いうちに他の扉を閉じてしまうことを禁じる決まりだ、と述べている。正解は「早く選ぶこと自体は否定しない」「他の道を開けておく」という二点を言い換えている。
【根拠】It is not a rule against choosing but a rule against closing the other doors while the child is still too young to know which one they will want.
【他の選択肢】
① Children should be kept out of organized competition altogether until they are old enough to explain why they want to take part in it. … "Children should be kept out of organized competition altogether" — 競技への参加そのものを遅らせよという主張は本文にない。本文が勧めているのは第二の競技・週の時間の上限・競技をしない期間である。
③ The decision belongs to the coach, since only someone who sees the squad every week can say whether more training would help the player. … "The decision belongs to the coach" — 本文は指導者が一季節の成績で評価される立場にあり、子ども時代の全体を見ているのは保護者だけだと述べており、判断を指導者に委ねよという主張とは逆である。
④ A child should be moved into a new sport every year so that no single set of joints is ever kept under load for more than one season. … "A child should be moved into a new sport every year" — 毎年競技を替えよとは本文のどこにも書かれておらず、本文の助言は主競技を続けたうえで第二の競技を年のどこかに残すというものである。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文空所補充
passages.title: Bridges from Retired Blades
passages.body:
Wind turbines produce electricity for decades, but their blades do not last forever. Most blades combine glass fiber with plastic resin. Because the materials are tightly bonded, this mixture is light and strong but difficult to separate into reusable materials. Blades can be cut into pieces, but this requires energy, and the material has limited uses. ( 1 ), many retired blades have been buried or stored. As wind farms built in the early 2000s reach retirement, more unwanted blades will appear.

Structural engineer Amira Voss wondered whether blades could remain useful without being broken apart. Their long, hollow shape reminded her of supporting beams under small bridges. Her team obtained retired blades, cut them to size, and tested sections under increasing pressure. The tests showed that the sections could ( 2 ). The researchers then designed a pedestrian bridge in which two blade sections carry a recycled-plastic walkway. A protective surface keeps rain from entering small cracks, while sensors monitor changes inside the material for signs of long-term damage.

Reusing blades this way will not solve the entire waste problem. Some are damaged, and transporting them far can be expensive. Nevertheless, a bridge may keep several tons of material out of a landfill and reduce the need for new beams. Blade models vary in dimensions, and individual blades have different service histories. ( 3 ) Voss therefore asks manufacturers for detailed records on older blades before approving their use. Bridges cannot replace the development of recyclable turbine materials, she says, but they can extend the value of existing products.
passages.body_ja:
風力発電機は何十年も電気を生み出せますが、その羽根が永久に使えるわけではありません。羽根の多くはガラス繊維とプラスチック樹脂を組み合わせて作られています。材料同士が強固に結び付いているため、この混合物は軽くて丈夫ですが、再利用可能な材料へ分離するのは困難です。羽根を細かく切ることはできますが、その工程にはエネルギーが必要で、得られた材料の用途も限られています。このため、多くの使用済み羽根は埋め立て処分されるか保管されてきました。2000年代初めに建設された風力発電所が耐用期間の終わりを迎えるにつれ、不要な羽根がさらに現れるでしょう。

構造技術者のアミラ・ヴォスは、羽根を分解せずに活用し続けられないかと考えました。細長く中が空洞になった形が、小さな橋の下にある支持梁を思わせたのです。彼女のチームは使用済みの羽根を入手し、適切な大きさに切り、各部分にかける圧力を徐々に増やして試験しました。その結果、羽根の部分が歩行者による大きな荷重を支えられることが分かりました。その後、研究者たちは、2本の羽根の一部で再生プラスチック製の歩道を支える歩道橋を設計しました。保護用の表面加工で小さなひびから雨が入るのを防ぎ、センサーで長期的な損傷の兆候がないか材料内部の変化を監視します。

この方法で羽根を再利用しても、廃棄物問題全体を解決できるわけではありません。損傷した羽根もあり、遠くまで運ぶと費用がかさむこともあります。それでも、橋なら数トンの材料が埋め立てられるのを防ぎ、新しい梁の必要も減らせる可能性があります。羽根の型によって寸法が異なり、個々の羽根の使用履歴もさまざまです。そのため、設計は入手できる羽根に合わせなければなりません。そこでヴォスは、利用を承認する前に古い羽根の詳しい記録を提供するよう製造業者へ求めています。橋への転用は、再利用可能な風力発電機材料の開発に代わるものではありませんが、既存製品の価値を長く保つことができると彼女は述べています。

questions.stem: ( 1 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: Even so
Similarly
For this reason
By accident
questions.explanation:
正解 ③ For this reason
分離が難しく、切断後の用途も限られることを原因として、多くの羽根が埋立て・保管されてきたという結果を導くため For this reason が適切。1 Even so は逆接、2 Similarly は並列比較、4 By accident は偶然を示すが、いずれも前後の因果関係を表せない。

questions.stem: ( 2 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: support heavy pedestrian loads
generate electricity underground
soften in cold weather
replace every bridge component
questions.explanation:
正解 ① support heavy pedestrian loads
could の後には動詞原形で始まる句が必要で、直前の increasing pressure による構造試験を受け、歩道橋の荷重を支えられるという結果が直後の橋の設計へつながる。2の地下発電は試験目的と無関係。3の低温軟化は記述がない。4は橋に歩道など別部材もあるため every bridge component と矛盾。

questions.stem: ( 3 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: A standard design can fit every retired blade.
Governments must import blades for every bridge.
Most projects can avoid transporting the blades.
Each design must suit the blades available.
questions.explanation:
正解 ④ Each design must suit the blades available.
直前に型ごとに寸法や使用履歴が異なるとあるため、入手した羽根に合わせた個別設計が必要となる。1の標準設計は正反対。2の海外調達義務も、3の輸送不要も本文に根拠がない。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文空所補充
passages.title: Listening to a Forest's Recovery
passages.body:
Reforestation projects are often judged by counting how many young trees survive. That information is useful, but it does not reveal whether insects, birds, and other animals are returning. Traditional wildlife surveys also have limitations: observers may miss animals that are active at night or hide in thick leaves. To obtain a broader picture, ecologists are placing small audio recorders in recovering forests. As a result, a single device can capture bird calls, frog songs, and insect sounds at different hours for months.

Researchers compare these recordings with the “soundscapes” of older, healthier forests nearby. A site with a growing variety of sounds may be recovering ecological functions, not just tree cover. Computer programs can search thousands of hours of audio for particular patterns, but the task is not automatic. Heavy rain may resemble the calls of some insects, and a program trained in one region may misidentify species elsewhere. Researchers therefore ( 1 ). Such checks also reveal unfamiliar calls that a computer has not learned to recognize.

Audio monitoring is becoming cheaper, allowing local communities to participate. In one project, students build weatherproof recorder cases and help create maps showing where certain bird calls first reappear. Still, sound alone can be misleading. A bird may fly over a recorder without living in the forest, while a silent species may be present but undetected. ( 2 ) Used carefully, however, sound recordings can alert conservationists to changes much sooner than occasional visual surveys. They also preserve evidence that can be reexamined when improved identification tools become available.
passages.body_ja:
森林再生事業は、若木が何本生き残ったかを数えることで評価されることがよくあります。その情報は有用ですが、昆虫や鳥などの動物が戻ってきているかどうかまでは分かりません。従来の野生生物調査にも限界があります。夜間に活動する動物や、茂った葉の中に隠れる動物を観察者が見落とすことがあるからです。より広い状況を把握するため、生態学者たちは再生中の森林に小型の録音機を設置しています。その結果、1台の機器で、異なる時間帯の鳥の鳴き声、カエルの声、昆虫の音を何か月にもわたって記録できます。

研究者たちは、こうした録音を、近くにあるより古く健全な森林の「音風景」と比較します。音の種類が増えている再生地では、木だけでなく、生態系の機能も回復しつつある可能性があります。コンピュータープログラムを使えば、何千時間分もの音声から特定のパターンを探せますが、作業を完全に自動化できるわけではありません。激しい雨音が一部の昆虫の声に似ている場合があり、ある地域のデータで学習したプログラムが別の地域の種を誤って識別することもあります。そのため、研究者は今も録音の一部を実際に聞き、プログラムが付けた分類を確認しています。この確認によって、コンピューターがまだ識別方法を学んでいない未知の鳴き声に気づくこともできます。

音声による監視は低価格になりつつあり、地域の人々も参加できるようになっています。ある取り組みでは、生徒が耐候性のある録音機ケースを作り、特定の鳥の声が最初に戻った場所を示す地図作りを手伝います。ただし、音だけでは誤解を招くことがあります。鳥がその森林にすんでいなくても録音機の上を飛ぶ場合がある一方、音を立てない種が存在しても検出されないことがあります。したがって、研究者は録音データを現地観察や植生調査と組み合わせるべきです。しかし注意して利用すれば、録音は、ときどき行う目視調査よりもはるかに早く変化を自然保護担当者に知らせられます。また、識別技術が向上したときに再検討できる証拠も残せます。

questions.stem: ( 1 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: verify labels by listening
trust every automatic label
remove rainfall before recording
avoid computers entirely
questions.explanation:
正解 ① verify labels by listening
Researchers therefore の後には動詞原形句が必要。雨音や地域差によってコンピューターが誤認するため、人が聞いて分類を確認する verify labels by listening が適切。2は自動分類を全面的に信頼するため逆。3は雨そのものを除去する非現実的内容。4はコンピューターとの併用を続けているため誤り。

questions.stem: ( 2 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: Visual surveys thus provide a complete record of forest species.
Only constantly calling animals should therefore guide restoration.
Recordings should therefore be combined with field and vegetation surveys.
Communities must consequently remove recorders from recovering forests.
questions.explanation:
正解 ③ Recordings should therefore be combined with field and vegetation surveys.
上空を通過しただけの鳥を定着種と誤認したり、静かな種を見落としたりするため、録音を現地観察・植生調査で補う必要がある。1は目視調査にも限界があるという第1段落と矛盾。2は保全対象を鳴き続ける動物だけに不当に限定する。4の機器撤去は、直後で録音の利点を述べる流れに反する。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文 内容一致
passages.title: What Counts at a Repair Café?
passages.body:
On the first Saturday of each month, a library in the town of Meriton fills with broken lamps, silent radios, and jackets with damaged zippers. Their owners bring them to a “repair café,” where volunteers with practical skills examine the objects. Instead of simply taking an item away and returning it later, the volunteers usually work beside its owner. They explain how to open a case safely, identify a loose connection, or replace a worn part. The service is free, although visitors may pay for replacement materials. When the program began, its organizers measured success by counting repaired objects. That number was easy to understand and helped them obtain a grant. Over time, however, they realized that it could be misleading.

Replacing a button in five minutes added one success to the total, while spending an hour diagnosing a rare appliance might not. Volunteers also refused to repair certain products, such as badly damaged heaters, because returning them to use could create a fire risk. Recording those cases simply as failures ignored the safety advice that visitors received. The organizers began asking visitors what they learned and what they did afterward. Six months after one event, many respondents said they had attempted another simple repair at home. Others reported that they now checked whether replacement parts were available before buying a product. Even when an object could not be saved, seeing why it had failed sometimes made its owner more willing to choose a durable model next time. These changes are difficult to express as a single number, but they may prevent more waste than repairing one inexpensive object.

The café also provides a social benefit. Retired technicians meet younger residents, and newcomers can participate without needing advanced language skills. Yet this success creates pressure. As attendance grows, volunteers may feel obliged to accept too many difficult jobs, and long waiting times can frustrate visitors. Meriton now uses an appointment system and limits each person to one object. It also offers short group lessons on common tasks, such as mending fabric or replacing a plug. The organizers still publish the number of objects repaired, but they present it alongside information about skills learned, unsafe products identified, and repeat visits. This broader account is less dramatic than claiming that every object can be rescued. It does, however, reflect the café's real purpose: not merely extending the life of possessions, but helping people make more informed decisions about what they own.
passages.body_ja:
メリトンという町では、毎月第1土曜日になると、図書館が壊れたランプ、音の出ないラジオ、ファスナーの傷んだ上着でいっぱいになります。持ち主たちはそれらを「リペア・カフェ」に持ち込み、実用的な技能を持つボランティアが品物を調べます。単に品物を預かって後で返すのではなく、ボランティアはたいてい持ち主の隣で作業します。そして、安全にケースを開ける方法、接続が緩んでいる箇所の見つけ方、傷んだ部品の交換方法などを説明します。交換材料の代金が必要な場合はありますが、サービスそのものは無料です。この取り組みを始めた当初、運営者は修理できた品物の数で成果を測っていました。その数字は分かりやすく、助成金を得るのにも役立ちました。しかし時間がたつにつれ、その数字が誤解を招くことに気づきました。

5分でボタンを交換しても成功1件と数えられる一方、珍しい家電の故障原因を1時間かけて調べても、成功として数えられないことがあります。また、大きく破損した暖房器具などは、再び使えるようにすると火災の危険があるため、ボランティアが修理を断りました。そうした事例を単なる失敗として記録すると、来場者が受け取った安全上の助言が無視されてしまいます。そこで運営者は、来場者が何を学び、その後どう行動したかを尋ねるようになりました。ある催しから6か月後、多くの回答者が自宅で別の簡単な修理に挑戦したと答えました。また、製品を買う前に交換部品を入手できるか確認するようになった人もいました。品物を救えなかった場合でも、故障の理由を目で確かめることで、次回はより丈夫な製品を選ぼうという気持ちになることがあります。こうした変化を一つの数字で表すのは困難ですが、安価な品物を一つ直すより多くの廃棄物を防ぐ可能性があります。

このカフェには社会的な利点もあります。退職した技術者が若い住民と出会い、新しく地域に来た人も高度な言語能力を必要とせず参加できます。しかし、その成功は負担も生みます。参加者が増えると、ボランティアが難しい依頼を過剰に引き受ける義務を感じることがあり、長い待ち時間は来場者をいら立たせます。そこでメリトンでは現在、予約制度を使い、一人につき品物一つに制限しています。また、布の繕い方やプラグの交換など、よくある作業について短い集団講習も開いています。運営者は今も修理できた品物の数を公表していますが、それに加えて、身についた技能、見つかった危険な製品、再訪者についての情報も示しています。この幅広い報告は、あらゆる品物を救えると主張するほど印象的ではありません。しかしそれは、単に所有物の寿命を延ばすだけでなく、自分の持ち物について人々がよりよい判断を下せるようにするという、カフェの本当の目的を表しています。

questions.stem: Why did the Meriton organizers stop relying only on the number of repaired objects?
choices: The number was too difficult for visitors and grant providers to understand.
It failed to reflect differences in effort and the value of safety advice.
Volunteers had begun reporting successful repairs as unsuccessful ones.
Most visitors refused to say whether their objects had been repaired.
questions.explanation:
正解 ② It failed to reflect differences in effort and the value of safety advice.
第1段落末から第2段落冒頭では、短時間のボタン交換も、長時間かけて原因だけを特定した作業も、単純な件数では同じか後者が失敗扱いになると説明している。さらに危険な製品の修理を断って安全助言をしても件数に表れない。1は件数が分かりやすかったという本文と逆。3・4は記述がない。

questions.stem: What did the follow-up questions reveal about some visitors?
choices: They preferred buying inexpensive products even when parts were unavailable.
They stopped attending because they were required to become volunteers.
They applied what they had learned to later repairs and purchasing decisions.
They believed that unsuccessful repairs should never be discussed publicly.
questions.explanation:
正解 ③ They applied what they had learned to later repairs and purchasing decisions.
追跡質問から、自宅で別の修理を試した人や、購入前に交換部品を確認するようになった人がいたと分かった。1は durable な製品を選ぶ方向と逆。2は参加停止やボランティア義務の記述がない。4も、修理不能の理由を知る学習効果と逆。

questions.stem: Which statement best expresses the main point of the passage?
choices: Repair cafés should accept every object in order to reduce as much waste as possible.
The social value of repair cafés disappears when an appointment system is introduced.
Repair cafés are effective only when professional technicians are paid to manage them.
The impact of a repair café includes learning and safer choices, so measuring success requires broader criteria.
questions.explanation:
正解 ④ The impact of a repair café includes learning and safer choices, so measuring success requires broader criteria.
本文は、修理件数だけでは学習、安全な判断、将来の購買行動、交流などを測れないため、幅広い指標が必要だと論じる。1は危険な製品を断る方針に反する。2は予約制導入後も社会的価値を否定していない。3は有給専門職だけが有効だとは述べていない。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文 内容一致
passages.title: A More Intelligent Kind of Darkness
passages.body:
Historically, brighter streets were treated as a sign of progress. Electric lighting extended business hours and aided travel after sunset. Efficient LEDs have made illumination cheaper, but lower costs have encouraged users to install more lights or operate them longer. Thus, efficient technology has not always produced darker skies or lower total electricity use. These effects can occur even when individual lamps consume little power. Scientists worry because darkness is an environmental condition, not merely an absence of daytime. Many insects navigate by natural light sources. Bright lamps can trap them in circles, leaving less time for feeding and reproduction. Some plants adjust flowering according to night length, while bats react differently: a few species hunt near lamps, but others avoid lit routes. Adding light may therefore benefit certain animals while dividing the habitat of others.

Reducing unnecessary illumination sounds simple, but officials must consider how people use each place. Residents may associate a brightly lit path with safety, although glare can make faces harder to see and sharp shadows hide hazards. Research on lighting and crime has produced mixed results, partly because locations differ. A busy station entrance, a quiet riverside path, and an empty office parking lot do not require identical treatment. The appropriate level also changes as traffic declines through the night. Applying the same reduction everywhere can create new problems. The town of Lydon therefore tested flexible lighting on a route between homes and a train station. Warm-colored LEDs pointed downward rather than toward trees. Before midnight, they operated at a moderate level. Later, they dimmed, but motion sensors temporarily brightened lamps ahead of pedestrians or cyclists. Biologists recorded more activity among light-sensitive bats, and electricity consumption fell. The route never became completely dark.

Initial surveys revealed some dissatisfaction. Sudden increases in brightness startled residents, and the gaps between activated lights made the path appear uneven. Engineers slowed the transition and programmed several lamps to brighten together. Residents also walked with planners to identify bushes blocking the view. These adjustments improved responses without returning to constant maximum brightness. The trial showed that acceptance depended not only on the amount of light but also on how predictably it behaved. Such systems still have limitations. Sensors and controls cost money, require maintenance, and may collect movement data. Cities need rules for what data are stored and for how long. They must also state whether the data can be shared with other agencies. They must ensure that unreliable equipment is not concentrated in neighborhoods with less political influence. Simple measures, including shields, timers, and removing useless lamps, may be preferable in many places.

The debate is therefore not a choice between flooding every street with light and leaving people in complete darkness. Policy begins by asking who needs light, when, and for what activity. Combining ecological observation with residents' experience can reveal where illumination is useful and where it is merely habitual. Cities can then treat darkness as a resource to manage carefully while still meeting practical human needs.
passages.body_ja:
歴史的に、明るい街路は進歩のしるしと考えられてきました。電灯によって店舗の営業時間が延び、人々は日没後も移動しやすくなりました。効率のよいLEDによって照明の費用は下がりましたが、そのため利用者が照明を増やしたり、より長く点灯したりするようにもなりました。したがって、省エネルギー技術が必ずしも夜空を暗くしたり、電力の総使用量を減らしたりしてきたわけではありません。個々の照明の消費電力が少なくても、こうした影響は起こり得ます。科学者が心配するのは、暗闇が単なる昼間の欠如ではなく、環境条件の一つだからです。多くの昆虫は自然の光源を頼りに移動します。明るい照明の周りを回り続け、食事や繁殖に使う時間が減ることがあります。一部の植物は夜の長さに応じて開花時期を調整します。一方、コウモリの反応は種によって異なり、照明の近くで狩りをする種もいれば、明るい経路を避ける種もいます。したがって、照明を加えることが一部の動物には役立つ一方、別の動物の生息地を分断する場合があります。

不要な照明を減らすのは簡単に思えますが、行政担当者は人々がそれぞれの場所をどう使うか考えなければなりません。まぶしさのために顔を見分けにくくなり、はっきりした影が危険な物を隠す場合でも、住民は明るい道を安全と結び付けることがあります。照明と犯罪に関する研究結果は一様ではなく、場所による違いがその一因です。利用者の多い駅の入口、静かな川沿いの道、無人のオフィス駐車場に同じ対策が必要なわけではありません。夜が更けて交通量が減るにつれて、適切な照度も変わります。どこでも同じように減光すれば、新たな問題を生む可能性があります。そこでリドンという町は、住宅地と鉄道駅を結ぶ道で柔軟な照明を試しました。暖色系のLEDを木々ではなく下方へ向け、真夜中までは適度な明るさにしました。それ以降は暗くなりますが、歩行者や自転車を感知すると、人の前方にある照明を一時的に明るくします。変更後、光に敏感なコウモリの活動が増え、電力消費量も減りました。道が完全に暗くなることはありませんでした。

それでも、最初の調査では一部に不満がありました。急に明るくなると住民が驚き、点灯した照明同士の間隔によって道の明るさが不均一に見えたのです。技術者は明るさの変化を遅くし、複数の照明が同時に明るくなるよう設定しました。住民も計画担当者と歩き、低木が視界を遮る場所を特定しました。こうした調整によって、常に最大の明るさへ戻さずに評価が改善しました。この試験は、受け入れられるかどうかが、光の量だけでなく、明るさの変化がどの程度予測可能かにも左右されることを示しました。このような仕組みにも限界があります。センサーや制御装置には費用と保守が必要で、人の移動データを集める可能性もあります。市は保存するデータと期間について規則を設け、他の機関と共有できるかどうかも明示しなければなりません。また、政治的な影響力が弱い地域に信頼性の低い機器が集中しないようにする必要があります。多くの場所では、遮光板、タイマー、不要な照明の撤去など、簡単な対策の方が望ましい場合もあります。

したがって、この議論は、あらゆる道路を光で満たすか、人々を完全な暗闇に置くかという二者択一ではありません。政策は、誰が、いつ、どのような活動のために光を必要とするのかを問うことから始まります。生態系の観察と住民の経験を組み合わせれば、照明が役立つ場所と、単に習慣で使われている場所を見分けられます。こうして都市は、実際の人間の必要を満たしながら、暗闇を注意深く管理すべき資源として扱えるのです。

questions.stem: Why does the passage mention the differing reactions of bats to artificial light?
choices: To show that all bat species become more active when insects gather near lamps
To illustrate that the same lighting change can affect species in different ways
To explain why bats are more reliable than insects as measures of electricity use
To argue that plants are less sensitive to the length of the night than bats are
questions.explanation:
正解 ② To illustrate that the same lighting change can affect species in different ways
照明近くで狩る種も、明るい経路を避ける種もいるという対照により、同じ照明でも種ごとに影響が異なることを示している。1は all として過度に一般化。3は電力測定との比較がない。4は植物とコウモリの感受性の強弱を論じていない。

questions.stem: What was learned from Lydon's lighting trial?
choices: Constant maximum brightness was necessary for residents to use the route.
Downward-facing lights reduced electricity use but ended all bat activity.
The system produced ecological benefits, and targeted adjustments improved public acceptance.
Residents preferred sensors that activated only one lamp with an immediate flash.
questions.explanation:
正解 ③ The system produced ecological benefits, and targeted adjustments improved public acceptance.
リドンではコウモリ活動と省電力という生態・エネルギー上の成果が得られ、住民の不満に対して点灯変化や同時点灯を調整すると評価も改善した。1は常時最大照度へ戻さず改善した点と矛盾。2は bat activity increased の逆。4は急な単独点灯が不評だったため逆。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what concern should cities address when introducing controlled lighting systems?
choices: The costs, data practices, and fair distribution of reliable equipment
The possibility that warm-colored LEDs will require more electricity than old lamps
The legal requirement to use network controls in every public parking lot
The risk that shields and timers will collect detailed movement information
questions.explanation:
正解 ① The costs, data practices, and fair distribution of reliable equipment
第3段落は、導入・保守費、人の移動データの保存・共有規則、政治力の弱い地域へ低品質設備を偏らせない公平性を課題として挙げる。2は暖色LEDの電力増加を述べない。3に法的義務はない。4はデータ収集の可能性があるのはセンサー等で、遮光板やタイマーとはされていない。

questions.stem: What approach to urban lighting does the author support?
choices: Applying an identical reduction in brightness to every neighborhood
Matching light to particular users, times, and places while considering nature
Keeping streets fully lit until research proves that darkness prevents crime
Replacing public consultation with automatic systems that react to movement
questions.explanation:
正解 ② Matching light to particular users, times, and places while considering nature
最終段落は、誰が・いつ・何のために光を必要とするかを問い、生態系の観察と住民経験を組み合わせるべきだと結論づける。1は一律削減の問題点に反する。3は常時全面照明を支持していない。4は住民参加を実際に重視しているため誤り。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文空所補充
passages.title: Counting the Trees We Cannot See
passages.body:
Many cities now invite residents to report street trees through smartphone apps. Volunteers photograph trunks, record species, and note signs of disease. The resulting maps may contain tens of thousands of entries, allowing researchers to examine urban forests at a scale that municipal staff could not achieve alone. Because every entry carries coordinates and a time stamp, the maps can look impressively exact.

( 1 ) volunteers tend to record trees along routes they already walk, while neighborhoods with fewer smartphone users receive less attention. Rare species also attract more photographs than common ones. Consequently, an unadjusted map may suggest that well-visited districts have healthier or more diverse tree populations, even when the pattern mainly reflects who supplied the data.

Researchers have developed ways to use such uneven records. ( 2 ) some teams compare volunteer reports with small, carefully selected survey plots. Others ask the app to record where participants looked but found no tree, information known as “absence data.” These methods allow analysts to estimate how much of the apparent pattern comes from observation habits rather than biology. The greatest strength of the project may appear only after several years. If instructions and categories remain consistent, repeated observations can reveal when trees flower, lose leaves, or suffer storm damage. ( 3 ) A single photograph cannot establish a trend, but thousands of comparable records collected season after season can show gradual change. Citizen observations, therefore, are neither automatically reliable nor merely amateur. Their value depends on researchers acknowledging bias, designing checks, and preserving the conditions that make comparisons meaningful.
passages.body_ja:
多くの都市が今では、住民にスマートフォンのアプリを通じて街路樹を報告してもらっている。ボランティアは幹を撮影し、樹種を記録し、病気の兆候を書き留める。こうしてできる地図には何万件もの記録が含まれることがあり、自治体職員だけでは不可能な規模で都市の樹木を研究できる。各記録には位置座標と時刻が付くため、地図は非常に正確に見えることがある。

しかし実際には、ボランティアは普段歩く経路沿いの木を記録しがちで、スマートフォン利用者の少ない地域には注意が向きにくい。また、珍しい樹種は普通の樹種より多く撮影される。その結果、調整していない地図では、よく訪問される地区ほど樹木が健康で多様に見えることがあるが、実際にはその傾向は主に誰がデータを提供したかを反映しているにすぎない場合がある。

研究者は、このような偏りのある記録を活用する方法を開発してきた。二つのパターンを切り分けるために、ボランティアの報告を、慎重に選んだ少数の調査区と比較するチームもある。また、参加者が探したが木を見つけなかった場所、すなわち「不在データ」もアプリに記録させる研究者もいる。こうした方法により、見かけ上の傾向のうち、どの程度が生物学的な違いではなく観察習慣から生じたのかを推定できる。この活動の最大の強みは、数年たって初めて現れるかもしれない。指示や分類が一貫していれば、繰り返しの観察から、木がいつ開花し、葉を落とし、嵐の被害を受けるかが分かる。一貫性が、ばらばらの報告を長期的な証拠へと変えるのである。1枚の写真だけでは傾向を立証できないが、季節ごとに集めた何千件もの比較可能な記録なら、徐々に進む変化を示せる。したがって、市民による観察は自動的に信頼できるわけでも、単なる素人仕事でもない。その価値は、研究者が偏りを認め、検証方法を設け、比較を有意義にする条件を維持できるかにかかっている。

questions.stem: ( 1 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: Accordingly,
Likewise,
In reality, however,
Furthermore,
questions.explanation:
正解 ③ In reality, however,
直前では座標や時刻により地図が正確に見えると述べるが、直後では観察経路や利用者分布による偏りを説明しており、In reality, however, が見かけと実態の逆接を示す。1 Accordingly は因果、2 Likewise は類似、4 Furthermore は単純な追加なので論理関係が合わない。

questions.stem: ( 2 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: To separate the two patterns,
To reward frequent contributors,
To eliminate common species,
To avoid all comparisons,
questions.explanation:
正解 ① To separate the two patterns,
後続の調査区との比較と不在データの記録は、観察者の行動による偏りと実際の生育傾向という二つのパターンを分離するための方法である。2の常連参加者への報奨、3の普通種の排除、4の比較回避はいずれも後続例の目的ではない。

questions.stem: ( 3 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: Consistency turns scattered reports into long-term evidence.
Thus, old records must be deleted before each survey.
More participants therefore make the project less accurate.
Nevertheless, phones cannot record flowering dates.
questions.explanation:
正解 ① Consistency turns scattered reports into long-term evidence.
直前の if instructions and categories remain consistent と、直後の comparable records collected season after season を橋渡しし、一貫性が長期的証拠を生むとまとめる。2は記録保存という目的に反し、3は参加増加で精度が下がるとは述べず、4は開花時期を観察できるという本文と矛盾する。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文空所補充
passages.title: Museums and the Missing Pieces
passages.body:
Museums use three-dimensional scanning to make digital models of damaged artifacts. A model can be rotated or enlarged to reveal tool marks. Visitors can handle a printed copy while the fragile original remains protected. Curators can test whether fragments in different institutions belonged to one object without transporting them.

Digital reconstruction involves more than recording surviving material. Software may fill cracks automatically, while a designer supplies the missing half of a symmetrical pattern. These additions are interpretations rather than direct observations. ( 1 ) viewers may assume every feature of a seamless model came from the original, although some portions are educated guesses. The more realistic the surface appears, the easier it is to overlook this distinction.

For that reason, several museums have begun attaching “uncertainty maps” to their models. ( 2 ) a dark region might represent scanned material, a lighter region a probable reconstruction, and an outline a highly speculative addition. Some institutions even allow users to switch proposed reconstructions on and off. This approach does not prevent interpretation; instead, it exposes the evidence behind it. Such transparency can also improve scholarship. When specialists disagree about the angle of a missing handle, the model can preserve several alternatives rather than forcing one permanent choice. Future discoveries can then be added without rebuilding the entire display. ( 3 ) A digital object is most informative when it shows both what experts know and where their knowledge ends. Used in this way, reconstruction does not disguise uncertainty. It turns uncertainty into something that researchers and the public can examine together.
passages.body_ja:
博物館は、三次元スキャンを使って損傷した遺物のデジタル模型を作る。模型は回転させたり、拡大して工具の痕跡を見せたりできる。壊れやすい実物を保護したまま、来館者には印刷した複製品に触れてもらえる。学芸員は、異なる施設にある破片がかつて一つの物体の一部だったかどうかを、破片を運ばずに検証できる。

デジタル復元は、現存資料を記録するだけではない。ソフトウェアが亀裂を自動的に埋め、デザイナーが左右対称の模様の失われた半分を補う場合がある。こうした追加は直接の観察ではなく解釈である。表示がなければ、見る人は継ぎ目のない模型のすべての特徴が実物由来だと思い込みかねないが、実際には一部が根拠に基づく推測である。表面が現実的に見えるほど、この違いは見落とされやすい。

そのため、複数の博物館が模型に「不確実性マップ」を添え始めている。確実性の程度を示すため、濃い部分はスキャン済みの材料、薄い部分は可能性の高い復元、輪郭だけの部分は推測性の高い追加を表す、といった具合である。提案された復元を利用者が表示・非表示に切り替えられる施設さえある。この方法は解釈を妨げるのではなく、その根拠を明らかにする。このような透明性は研究の向上にもつながる。失われた取っ手の角度について専門家の意見が分かれた場合、模型は一つを恒久的に選ぶ代わりに、複数の案を残せる。その後、新たな発見があれば展示全体を作り直さずに追加できる。したがって、目的は疑いようがないほど完全に見える模型を作ることではない。デジタル資料が最も有益なのは、専門家が何を知っているかと、その知識がどこで尽きるかの両方を示すときである。このように使えば、復元は不確実性を覆い隠さない。不確実性を、研究者と一般の人々が共に検討できるものへ変えるのである。

questions.stem: ( 1 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: For protection,
For accuracy,
With certainty,
Without labels,
questions.explanation:
正解 ④ Without labels,
直前で補完部分は直接観察ではなく解釈だと述べ、直後では来館者がそれを実物と誤認し得るため、Without labels, が条件を示す。1の保護目的、2の正確さ、3の確信をもって、はいずれも来館者の誤認が生じる条件にならない。

questions.stem: ( 2 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: To advertise scanning equipment,
To display degrees of certainty,
To restrict public access,
To record an artifact's ownership,
questions.explanation:
正解 ② To display degrees of certainty,
不確実性マップの濃淡や輪郭は、スキャン部分・可能性の高い復元・推測性の高い追加という『確実性の程度』を示す。1は機材広告、3は公開制限、4は所有権記録であり、次文の凡例と対応しない。

questions.stem: ( 3 ) に入れるのに最も適切なものを選びなさい。
choices: Physical artifacts will consequently become unnecessary.
Only one reconstruction should be shown publicly.
The goal is not an unquestionably complete-looking model.
Published models should never be revised.
questions.explanation:
正解 ③ The goal is not an unquestionably complete-looking model.
複数案を保存して将来更新できるという前文を受け、完全に見せることより知識の限界を示すべきだという次文につなぐ。1は実物不要と飛躍し、2は複数案の保存と矛盾し、4は将来の発見による更新を否定するため不適切。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文 内容一致
passages.title: A Map Made of Sound
passages.body:
In some cities, a large share of treated water is lost before reaching customers. Much of it escapes through small underground leaks that never produce a visible puddle. Utilities traditionally search for these leaks by dividing a network into zones and watching for unexplained changes in water flow. Crews may then walk streets with listening equipment, but inspecting thousands of kilometers of pipe is slow and expensive. Locating them early matters because pumping and purifying replacement water consumes energy, while prolonged leakage can weaken nearby roads. Several utilities are now attaching inexpensive acoustic sensors to valves and hydrants. Water escaping under pressure creates vibrations that travel along a pipe. A sensor records these vibrations at night, when traffic and household water use are relatively low, and software compares the signal with earlier recordings. Persistent sounds at particular frequencies can indicate a leak. By collecting readings over many nights, the system can distinguish a continuing vibration from a passing truck or a brief surge in demand.

The sensors do not, however, produce a simple map of holes. The same leak sounds different in an iron pipe and a plastic one, while compact soil transmits vibrations differently from loose soil. Pumps, building machinery, and even insects can create misleading signals. An algorithm trained in one district may therefore perform poorly in another. In a trial in northern England, the software successfully identified several leaks but also repeatedly marked a street where an underground ventilation fan operated after midnight.

Rather than abandoning the system, the utility changed how it used the results. Engineers added information about pipe material, installation date, and previous repairs. The software then ranked sites according to the likelihood of a leak, and experienced technicians reviewed the highest-ranked locations before crews began digging. This reduced unnecessary excavation without treating the algorithm's judgment as proof. Acoustic monitoring is sometimes promoted as a technology that will automate maintenance. Its more realistic contribution may be less dramatic: it directs scarce human attention. A sensor network can observe far more locations than a team can visit, but technicians understand local construction practices and recognize unusual sources of noise. When the two kinds of knowledge are combined, utilities can repair leaks sooner and avoid digging in the wrong place. The system is valuable not because it removes people from the decision, but because it changes which decisions deserve their time.
passages.body_ja:
一部の都市では、処理された水のかなりの割合が利用者に届く前に失われている。その多くは、地上に水たまりを作ることのない小さな地下漏水から逃げている。水道事業者は従来、配管網を区域に分け、水量の説明できない変化を監視して漏水を探してきた。その後、作業員が聴音装置を持って通りを歩くこともあるが、何千キロもの配管を調べるのは時間も費用もかかる。早期発見が重要なのは、代わりの水を送り浄化するのにエネルギーが必要であり、漏水が長引けば近くの道路が弱くなることもあるからだ。現在、複数の水道事業者が、バルブや消火栓に安価な音響センサーを取り付けている。圧力下で漏れる水は、配管に沿って伝わる振動を生む。交通量と家庭での水使用が比較的少ない夜間にセンサーが振動を記録し、ソフトウェアが過去の記録と信号を比較する。特定の周波数で持続する音は漏水の兆候になり得る。何晩にもわたって測定値を集めれば、継続する振動と、通過するトラックや一時的な需要の急増とを区別できる。

しかし、センサーが穴の位置を単純な地図にしてくれるわけではない。同じ漏水でも鉄管と樹脂管では音が異なり、締まった土と緩い土でも振動の伝わり方が違う。ポンプ、建物の機械、さらには昆虫でさえ紛らわしい信号を生むことがある。そのため、ある地区で学習したアルゴリズムが別の地区ではうまく働かない場合がある。イングランド北部の実証試験では、ソフトウェアはいくつかの漏水を正しく特定した一方、深夜に地下換気扇が動く通りを繰り返し漏水地点として示した。

水道事業者はシステムを放棄するのではなく、結果の使い方を変えた。技術者は配管の材質、設置時期、過去の修理に関する情報を加えた。次にソフトウェアが漏水の可能性に従って場所を順位づけし、掘削開始前に経験豊富な技術者が上位の場所を確認した。これにより、アルゴリズムの判断を証明済みの事実として扱うことなく、不要な掘削を減らせた。音響監視は、保守作業を自動化する技術として宣伝されることがある。しかし、より現実的な貢献はそれほど劇的ではなく、限りある人間の注意を向ける先を定めることかもしれない。センサーネットワークはチームが訪問できるよりはるかに多くの場所を観察できるが、技術者は地域の施工慣行を理解し、特殊な騒音源も見分ける。二種類の知識を組み合わせれば、水道事業者は漏水を早く修理し、誤った場所を掘ることを避けられる。このシステムが有益なのは、人間を意思決定から外すからではなく、どの判断に人間の時間を使う価値があるかを変えるからである。

questions.stem: What is one purpose of collecting acoustic readings over many nights?
choices: To separate a persistent leak signal from temporary sources of vibration
To calculate how many customers use water in each district
To test whether treated water contains harmful chemicals
To prevent valves and hydrants from corroding underground
questions.explanation:
正解 ① To separate a persistent leak signal from temporary sources of vibration
第2段落末で、複数夜の記録により continuing vibration と passing truck / brief surge を区別できると明記される。2は顧客数、3は水質、4は腐食防止で、いずれも音響記録の目的ではない。

questions.stem: Why did the utility add pipe data and technician review to the system?
choices: The sensors had stopped recording vibrations after midnight.
National regulations prohibited fully automated nighttime monitoring.
Local materials and noise sources made the software's raw predictions uncertain.
The utility wanted the algorithm to identify insects rather than leaks.
questions.explanation:
正解 ③ Local materials and noise sources made the software's raw predictions uncertain.
管材や土質、機械・昆虫などによって音が変わり、別地区でアルゴリズムが誤る例が示される。そのため配管情報と経験者の確認を加えた。1は記録停止の記述がなく、2は規制の話がなく、4は昆虫を漏水と誤認しないためであって昆虫検出が目的ではない。

questions.stem: What does the author suggest about the main value of acoustic monitoring?
choices: It can eliminate the need for workers with knowledge of local construction.
It can help people decide where their limited inspection effort is most useful.
It proves that algorithms trained in one location work equally well everywhere.
It is most effective when every high-ranked site is excavated immediately.
questions.explanation:
正解 ② It can help people decide where their limited inspection effort is most useful.
最終段落の directs scarce human attention と changes which decisions deserve their time が中心。1は技術者の地域知識が必要という本文に反し、3は地区間で性能が落ちる記述と逆、4は掘削前に人が確認して不要な掘削を減らす方法と矛盾する。

passages.unit: 準1級 長文 内容一致
passages.title: Restoring for an Uncertain Future
passages.body:
Throughout the twentieth century, ecological restoration had a straightforward goal: return a damaged place to an earlier condition. Practitioners examined records and nearby undisturbed sites to decide which species belonged. “Reference ecosystems” remain useful. They reveal whether a valley supported grassland or woodland, and they prevent restoration from becoming an arbitrary exercise in planting fast-growing species. Yet a historical target can imply that environmental conditions are stationary. A forest assembled under the rainfall and temperature patterns of a century ago may not survive those expected fifty years from now. Fire regimes have changed, soils have been altered, and some pollinators have disappeared. Even if practitioners reproduce the old list of species, the relationships that sustained the ecosystem might no longer exist. Ecosystems depend on timing and interaction, and climate projections describe ranges rather than a certain future.

One response is assisted migration: moving populations or species from warmer or drier regions into places suited to future conditions. Supporters argue that restoration should prepare for anticipated change rather than recreate the past. Critics warn that introduced organisms may spread, compete with local populations, or bring disease. There is also a cultural concern. Communities may value plants with which they have long-standing relationships, so replacing them with supposedly climate-ready species can turn a technical project into a dispute over whose idea of the landscape counts.
